- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and prices are trending down, model underestimates drop; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to account for volatility.
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops after 10–15 days of downward momentum; apply 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment for 30-day horizon if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment shift.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), model often fails to capture it; adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5 days if sentiment is negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 1.00 values (strong bullish), model tends to overfit recent highs; apply downward bias of 2–3% for 3–5 days after peak.
